Bo-Katan, disordered by Vizsla's death, frantically told Maul that no outsider would ever rule Mandalore and called those who knelt to him traitors, but Maul dismissed her protests and bluntly told her that history would not see it that way. He ordered the Death Watch warriors loyal to him to execute Bo-Katan and the other dissenters, but they managed to flee the palace after a firefight. Maintaining his plan to establish a criminal underworld using Mandalore as a front, Maul gave Almec the position of prime minister. As prime minister, Almec, having long abandoned his New Mandalorian beliefs, adopted Vizsla's declaration that the warrior ways would return. In public, Almec covered for Vizsla's death and Duchess Satine's continued imprisonment by falsely claiming that Kryze had murdered Vizsla, that she was under arrest for the killing, and that it was Vizsla's last command that Almec be reinstated as prime minister. He further promoted the Death Watch's propaganda, remembering Vizsla as a martyr who had saved the Mandalorians in time of need while Satine had fled. Behind Almec's artificial patriotism, however, he and Maul moved forward with the repression of the Mandalorian people.''[[Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy]]'' Where Vizsla had targeted political opponents, Maul and Almec placed all of Sundari under lockdown and cut communication frequencies into the city. In the meantime, Bo-Katan and her fellow dissenters resolved to remove Maul from power. Her faith in the Death Watch shaken, Bo-Katan decided to reconcile with her long-estranged sister, Duchess Satine, and [[Mandalore resistance|allied]] with a militant group of Satine's followers, led by their nephew [[Korkie Kryze]].{{TCW|The Lawless}} [[File:KryzeRecruitsTano-TA.png|thumb|left|250px|Resolving to remove Maul from the throne, Bo-Katan Kryze sought Republic help to lay siege to Mandalore.]] Bo-Katan and Korkie led an attempt to rescue Satine from prison, but the duchess was recaptured after sending a plea for help to Obi-Wan Kenobi. As a result of Kryze's neutrality and a report from Ahsoka Tano about her skirmish with Vizsla on Carlac that the Death Watch had no ties to the Confederacy, however, Kenobi was forced to go to Mandalore undercover without Republic backing. Despite his deal with Vizsla to kill Kenobi, Maul murdered Satine in front of the Jedi instead, wanting the slaying of his enemy's beloved to make Kenobi suffer. Bo-Katan rescued Kenobi from Maul's forces, an act that led to an [[Mandalorian Civil War (19 BBY)|all-out war]] between her resistance and the [[Mandalorian super commando|remnants]] of Death Watch loyal to the Sith. With Satine's execution, Maul delivered a fatal blow to what remained of the New Mandalorians, fulfilling the late Vizsla's lifelong goal. Maul's rule was briefly interrupted by his former Sith master, Darth Sidious, as well as Sidious' replacement apprentice, Dooku. As a result, the Shadow Collective and Confederacy entered a [[Campaign against the Shadow Collective|brief war]].[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 1|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 1]] During the conflict between Maul's forces and the Confederacy, the base Pre Vizsla had established on Zanbar was [[Battle of Zanbar|decimated]], and Maul was forced to use Vizsla Keep 09,[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 3|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 3]] a secret outpost the Death Watch created earlier in the Clone Wars, to hold hostage Separatist leaders. Bo-Katan's resistance informed the Republic of this, and a Jedi-led task force [[Assault on Vizsla Keep 09|assaulted]] Vizsla Keep 09 but failed to bring Maul to justice. Maul would eventually [[Second Battle of Dathomir|lose]] his conflict with the Sith and the Confederacy,[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 4|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 4]] after which he secretly returned to Sundari,{{TCW|Old Friends Not Forgotten}} where he maintained the loyalty of the Death Watch and the Shadow Collective. Among Maul's leading commandos were [[Gar Saxon]]{{TCW|The Phantom Apprentice}} and [[Rook Kast]], who was among the first to embrace Maul and change the colors of her armor from those under Vizsla's rule to those reflecting her devotion to Maul.{{SWCT|set=2020 Base Series 2|cardname=Rook Kast}} With aid from Ahsoka Tano, by then no longer a Jedi, Bo-Katan's resistance was able to locate Maul and convince the Republic to aid them in a [[siege of Mandalore]] near the war's end, which resulted in Maul and his forces removal from power.{{TCW|Shattered}} ====The Imperial Age and beyond==== {{Quote|Are you Death Watch?''"
"''Death Watch exists no longer. It shattered into many warring factions.|A Mandalorian captain and a Mandalorian [[The Armorer|Armorer]]|{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 23: The Spies}}}} After successfully ousting Maul during the siege of Mandalore, Bo-Katan was named the planet's regent by the Republic, but her reign was cut short when the Republic transformed into the authoritarian Galactic Empire at the end of the Clone Wars. Refusing to acquiesce, Kryze was effectively removed from office and replaced with Saxon, who pledged loyalty to the Empire, which occupied Mandalore.''[[Star Wars Rebels: Heroes of Mandalore]]'' In the decades after the Empire's formation, various Mandalorian sects chose to integrate themselves with the Empire out of necessity,{{Rebels|Legacy of Mandalore}} including groups formerly aligned with the opposing beliefs of Pre Vizsla and Satine Kryze.{{Rebels|The Protector of Concord Dawn}} Despite sharing common disdain for the Empire, tensions existed between these groups long after the Clone Wars, and the late Vizsla and his nemesis had polarizing legacies. Although Mandalore largely returned to its warrior ways, Satine's rule had undergone reconsideration, with even Vizsla's former lieutenant Bo-Katan looking back on her sister's ambitions with appreciation and repentance. [[File:Bo-Katan-Darksaber.png|thumb|right|250px|Bo-Katan Kryze raises the Darksaber to unite the Mandalorians against the Galactic Empire, becoming the first Mand'alor since Pre Vizsla's death.]] Under Saxon's leadership, Death Watch propaganda from Vizsla's lifetime was destroyed.''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]'' During conflict between Saxon and [[Clan Wren]], which had been aligned with the Death Watch, Saxon was murdered by Countess [[Ursa Wren]], a former member of the Nite Owls. The act spurred a [[Mandalorian Civil War (Imperial Era)|war]] between [[Clan Saxon]] and Clan Wren and eventually led to another civil war. Bo-Katan joined Clan Wren and accepted the Darksaber from [[Sabine Wren]], who had retrieved the legendary sword from the late Maul's [[Nightsister lair|lair]] a [[2 BBY|year prior]]. Wielding the Darksaber, Kryze united various clans and formed a resistance to the Empire in the name of her sister. Among the clans that joined her was Clan Vizsla, which had replaced the ''[[Shriek-hawk|jai'galaar]]'' symbol''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' used by Pre Vizsla with a peacetime sigil predating the Death Watch. Kryze's attempt to repel the Empire would lead to failure, with the occupiers enacting the genocide of the Mandalorian people and the decimation of the planet's surface in the [[Great Purge of Mandalore|Great Purge]]. Many years later, after the Empire's fall, Kryze rallied surviving Mandalorians of various creeds to [[Conflict on Mandalore|return]] to the Mandalore, which they resettled.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 24: The Return}} In the [[New Republic Era]], long after the Clone Wars, [[Exantor Divo]], grandson of [[Tanivos Exantor Divo|Tanivos Divo]], a member of the Coruscant Security Force during the Clone Wars, received his father's lost case files. Among the files was one detailing the Shadow Collective's coup against the New Mandalorians. As Exantor learned from his grandfather's documents, Republic Intelligence had known of Vizsla's involvement with the brief criminal alliance.''[[Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]'' At some point after Vizsla's death, accounts of his life were depicted on a series of illustrated maps by the [[Ithorian]] [[artist]] [[Gammit Chond]]. Although he was a recluse, Chond purportedly based his maps on stories he heard from travelers, including those of Vizsla's campaign and his brief reign and death at the hands of Maul. Long after they were created, the maps, which were among what little of Chond's artwork to survive, were stored in the [[Shadow Stacks]] of the [[Graf Archive]] on the moon [[Orchis 2]] until a [[Unidentified archivist student (Gammit Chond's maps)|student archivist]] exhumed the set, after which they were painstakingly restored and released as a collection. According to{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Chrome Perspectives|subset=Sith Information Guide|cardname=Pre Vizsla|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/114595/cid/8022697/2015-Topps-Chrome-Star-Wars-Perspectives-Jedi-vs.-Sith-43-S-Pre-Vizsla}} false claims from the [[Sith Information Guide]], Vizsla survived the Clone Wars and served as a willing ally to the Empire. In his retrospective overview of Mandalorian history, "[[Mandalorians Through the Ages]]," a supplemental guide to the tenth edition of ''[[Mandalorian Battlefield Tours]]'', [[historian]] [[Eloc Throno]] described the ideological conflict between Pre Vizsla and Satine Kryze in detail. Although Throno opined that Kryze's reform efforts were largely vindicated, he admitted that Vizsla had successfully challenged the merit of the New Mandalorian experiment during the Clone Wars. Throno also noted that Vizsla's coup against Kryze and the New Mandalorians was successful in part because he had built himself and the Death Watch into folk heroes, an image that helped the Mandalorian people accept and celebrate the false reality that Vizsla was a liberator. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|I believed you had honor, but you're just a murderer. No better than Dooku.|Lux Bonteri, to Pre Vizsla|}} [[File:PreVizslaDetail-SWE.png|thumb|left|200px|Pre Vizla was proud of his heritage as a scion of Clan Vizsla.]] Pre Vizsla was a [[Gender|male]] [[human]] with light skin, blue [[eye]]s, and blond [[hair]] who stood at 1.84 [[meter]]s tall, or 6 [[Foot|feet]], and weighed 80 kilograms. During his tenure as Governor of Concordia, he kept his hair short and slicked back with an undercut. At some point after he was publicly revealed as the leader of the Death Watch, Vizsla began shaving his head, and his appearance grew unkempt as well. It was during this time that he also gained a distinct scar across his left cheek, the result of an altercation with Count Dooku. Claiming heritage to Tarre Vizsla, the ancient Mand'alor who first ruled using the Darksaber,{{InsiderCite|202|A Certain Point of View}} Pre Vizsla was deeply proud of his roots in Clan Vizsla and the traditions therein. Valorizing the Mandalorian tenants of strength and honor, Vizsla believed in the old ways of the "one ruler," a position he would eventually assert belonged to him despite the faded influence of the Darksaber, which he had inherited. Because of his ancestry and heritage, Vizsla was immediately opposed to the reformist New Mandalorian movement and soon harbored a deep enmity towards the political group's leader, Duchess Satine Kryze. Although he initially only believed she was unworthy to succeed her father, Vizsla grew to hate the woman for everything she stood for. He believed that her pacifist policies were unbecoming of a Mandalorian and that she had tarnished the reputation of their people. He held that Kryze had crushed the Mandalorian identity and soul, and considered her pacifism tantamount to a personal attack on everything he held dear. Vizsla professed strength, often as a way of contrasting himself and his warrior visage with what he considered the "weak-minded" rule of the New Mandalorians. Despite his self-ascribed hardiness, however, Vizsla sought his goals of reversing the reforms enacted by Kryze anxiously,{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Chrome Perspectives|subset=Sith Information Guide|cardname=Pre Vizsla|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/114595/cid/8022697/2015-Topps-Chrome-Star-Wars-Perspectives-Jedi-vs.-Sith-43-S-Pre-Vizsla}} a trait that grew more apparent as he kept failing to achieve them. Vizsla painted himself as an organized militant, but the failure of his first takeover attempt resulted in further cracks in his facade, revealing him to be little more than a cultish{{Topps|set=2021 Topps Star Wars Bounty Hunters|cardname=Pre Vizsla|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/263568/cid/18708459/2021-Topps-Star-Wars-Bounty-Hunters-B1-73-Pre-Vizsla}} zealot armed with a cruel temper,{{Databank|carlac|Carlac}} and his repeated humiliations by both Duchess Satine and Count Dooku damaged his mental state to the point some believed he had gone mad. Likewise, Vizsla's obsession with what he perceived to be a Mandalorian sense of honor had become hypocritical as he demonstrated brutality against those that disagreed with him as a show of strength, senselessly bullied, enslaved, and eventually slaughtered the Ming Po of Carlac, and enacted the executions of his political rivals once in power. [[File:Vizsla_brutal.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Though he believed he was an honorable warrior, Vizsla was an egotistical and cruel-tempered zealot.]] Narcissistically believing that he was carrying the traditions of his ancestors, Vizsla maintained opposition to the Jedi Order and the Galactic Republic, both of which had warred with the Mandalorians during the Old Republic Era. He considered these ancient enemies of Mandalore his personal enemies, and believed that the individual Jedi in the Order had to pay for the ancient wars, which he referred to as "crimes against Mandalore." To Vizsla, the payback he felt he was due to give the Jedi was a form of justice. He was willing to ally with anyone as long as they were enemies of the Jedi. Despite his passionate hatred of the Jedi, Vizsla was unwilling to give them an unfair fight, in part because of his egotistical view that his martial prowess could outmatch that of the Jedi. Vizsla's ego often got the better of him, however, leading to losses in duels with Obi-Wan Kenobi and Ahsoka Tano. His loss to Ahsoka Tano, in particular, resulted in rage from Vizsla, who seethed as she handily escaped his attempted execution of her. Unable to see the New Mandalorian government as a viable power, Vizsla continually misunderstood what it would take to overthrow it. In both his alliances with the Confederacy of Independent Systems and the Shadow Alliance, Vizsla failed to consider his enemies as anything more than the weak cowards he believed them to be. Through his interactions with the much more strategic Dooku and Darth Maul, the former of whom believed Vizsla's intelligence was none more than a "neophyte's," Vizsla displayed an inability to think out his plans or accept criticism. Maul's assertion that Vizsla had no material reason to replace Duchess Satine, in particular, insulted Vizsla's long and evangelistic belief that it was his purpose to do so. Similar to his ability to act cordially with Kryze as the Governor of Concordia, Vizsla managed to maintain appearances with Maul, enough that he could seize the Mandalorian throne, but his obsessive quest and adherence to his beloved warrior ways would lead him to his death. ==Skills and abilities== {{Quote|Stop! The Jedi is ''mine''.|Pre Vizsla, before dueling Ahsoka Tano|}} [[File:FirstSkirmishOnCarlac-AFIN.png|thumb|left|250px|Though not Force-sensitive, Vizsla was able to hold his own in combat with Force wielders such as Ahsoka Tano.]] A highly skilled warrior, Pre Vizsla was adept at various forms of combat. He was known for his excellent marksmanship and could expertly handle various ranged weaponry with ease, including the blasters embedded in his wrist gauntlets and his signature pistols. He was a very capable fighter in both armed and unarmed combat and could go up against much more powerful foes, including Force-sensitives. Though he was not as athletic as his Force-wielding enemies, such as Obi-Wan Kenobi and Darth Maul, Vizsla made up for his lack of agility with potent [[Unarmed combat|hand-to-hand combat]] abilities. In addition, Vizsla was a well-trained swordsman, a necessity for him to properly wield the Darksaber. Where others were unable to handle the Darksaber without difficulty,{{Rebels|Trials of the Darksaber}} Vizsla carried the saber with ease. Even if he could not match Jedi or Sith with his combat skills alone, Vizsla was able to hold his own in duels. By the time of his duel with Maul for the Mandalorian throne, Vizsla had mastered his ability to mix his martial capabilities and could swiftly alternate weaponry and skillsets as he needed. This dexterity allowed him to grow as a fighter and learn how to go toe-to-toe with Force wielders, shown when he was able to enter a prolonged fight with Maul, which contrasted with shorter duels with Kenobi and Ahsoka Tano. Though he lacked the intelligence of allies like Count Dooku and Maul or enemies like Duchess Satine, Vizsla had a strong propensity for leadership, using his strongman persona and passionate rhetoric to rally Mandalorians to his cause. Vizsla was also multilingual and could speak both Galactic Basic Standard and Mand'oa,{{BuildFalconCite|68|Starship Fact File}} though he, like most other Mandalorians during his time, primarily spoke using the former. ==Equipment== {{Quote|This lightsaber was stolen from your Jedi Temple by my ancestors during the fall of the Old Republic. Since then, many Jedi have died upon its blade. Prepare yourself to join them!|Pre Vizsla shows Obi-Wan Kenobi the Darksaber|audio=Darksaber-TMP.flac|}} [[File:Pre_Vizsla_Helmets.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Pre Vizsla's helmet.]] As a Mandalorian warrior, Vizsla wore the traditional and resilient [[Mandalorian armor|armor]] of his people.''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]'' Prior to the failure of his first attempt to take over Mandalore, Vizsla's armor featured a clean paint finish, with various shades of blue and gray, as well as several details painted with red and yellow, including the symbol of the shriek-hawk, which represented Clan Vizsla, on his helmet. Completing his armored appearance was a gray and blue serape, which was also adorned with the shriek-hawk. After his attempted coup fell apart the Death Watch was forced to relocate to Carlac. Vizsla's formerly clean armor became battered, and the various vibrant paints faded and worn away. While no longer wearing his [[cape]], Vizsla customized his armor still, adding antennae to his helmet, and his chest plates displayed a traditional Mandalorian design. Usually heavily armed, Vizsla's gear included a jetpack, [[magnet]]ized boots, and a pair of [[Mandalorian vambrace|armored vambraces]]. Like other Mandalorian vambraces, Vizsla's featured a variety of gadgets, including blaster barrels, a flamethrower, a whipcord launcher, and a launcher that fired disc-shaped buzz saws. [[File:Pre_Vizsla_Darksaber_SW.png|thumb|left|210px|Heavily armed and armored, Vizsla utilized various weapons and gadgets in battle, including the fabled Darksaber.]] In addition to two [[WESTAR-35 blaster pistol]]s, which he kept in hip [[holster]]s, one of Vizsla's most prized weapons was the Darksaber, an ancient lightsaber crafted by his ancestor Tarre Vizsla and passed down to him through several generations of Clan Vizsla. A one-of-a-kind artifact, the Darksaber had a long and storied history among the Mandalorians. Although diminished by the time Vizsla inherited it, the Darksaber served as a symbol of authority for his people, and by tradition, whoever wielded it was the rightful ruler of the Mandalore. Though the Darksaber was similar to the Jedi lightsaber, it was unique in shape and color. The Darksaber's signature flat energy blade, which had an angled point near its tip like some metal swords, emitted from a narrow slit in the saber's rectangular hilt. When activated, the black energy blade crackled and was outlined by white plasma energy.''[[Star Wars: The Lightsaber Collection]]'' Vizsla used the Darksaber as his personal weapon, and had an attachment to his jetpack that allowed him to store it there when not in use. By 19 BBY, Vizsla owned a ''Kom'rk''-class Mandalorian fighter, simply christened [[Gauntlet (Pre Vizsla)|''Gauntlet'']], a name commonly used to describe ''Kom'rk'' fighters in general. Vizsla's ship was also called by a name in Mand'oa that translated to ''Gauntlet'' in Galactic Basic Standard. Like other ''Kom'rk'' ships utilized by the Death Watch, the ''Gauntlet'' was designed and built in secret by engineers and technicians loyal to the faction. Vizsla had the ''Gauntlet'' proudly finished with the Mandalorian colors of white, blue, and gray, reflecting the traditional colors used in his armor. The ''Gauntlet'' measured 52.3 meters in length and followed the sleek, if peculiar, configuration commonly used in Mandalorian ship design. After the Death Watch settled on Zanbar, Vizsla and his crew used the ''Gauntlet'' as part of his campaigns, taking it into deep space for explorations and using it in missions to Mustafar, Nal Hutta, and eventually, Mandalore, where Vizsla used it as his base of operations during his coup against the New Mandalorians. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|I thought it would be a really cool thing for Jon, and fun for fans if he did the part. And he did a great job of playing Pre Vizsla; he's the one guy that, in this whole Mandalorian world, is the defender of the historic Mandalorian past. He's the one character who knows what the Mandalorians were and what they should be, and wants to get them back to that reality. He's a great character and I think that he'll become a favorite of many fans.|Series Director Dave Filoni, on casting Jon Favreau in the role of Pre Vizsla|{{InsiderCite|115|Ready for Battle!}}}} Pre Vizsla first appeared as the primary antagonist in "[[The Mandalore Plot]]," the twelfth episode of the [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]] of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''. The episode was directed by [[Kyle Dunlevy]], written by [[Melinda Hsu]] and [[Drew Z. Greenberg]], and first aired on Cartoon Network on [[January 29]], [[2010]].{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode212.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: The Mandalore Plot}} "The Mandalore Plot" serves as the first episode of a three-part story arc, followed by "Voyage of Temptation" and "Duchess of Mandalore," which explores the Mandalorian civilization at the time of the Clone Wars. "Voyage of Temptation" was initially the only planned episode of the trilogy,{{InsiderCite|117|The Duchess and the Jedi}} but when series creator [[George Lucas]], at the insistence of [[Dave Filoni]] and [[Henry Gilroy]], decided to expand on the storyline and feature more of the Mandalorians in ''The Clone Wars'', "The Mandalore Plot" was written. Vizsla featured heavily in promotional material for the episodes, with several mentions in the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine and clips of "The Mandalore Plot" shown at the [[2009]] [[Wikipedia:San Diego Comic-Con|San Diego Comic Con International]]. [[File:Serape.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Pre Vizsla's concept model sheet shows the Mandalorian symbol on his cape.]] Vizsla is voiced in ''The Clone Wars'' by [[Wikipedia:American|American]] director [[Jon Favreau]], who was cast when Filoni learned that he was a fan of Star Wars. The two met at [[Skywalker Ranch]] while Favreau was working on the [[2008]] film [[Wikipedia:Iron Man|''Iron Man'']]. While showing Filoni some of his work on ''Iron Man'', Favreau mentioned off-hand that he was interested in voicing a character in ''The Clone Wars'', and it happened that the role of Vizsla had not been cast yet. The part marked Favreau's first contribution to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' franchise, and he would later create the live-action television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]''.{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/05/star-wars-cover-the-rebellion-will-be-televised|text=''Star Wars:'' The Rebellion Will Be Televised|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archivedate=20220517110251|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2022-05-17}} Favreau reprised the role of Vizsla in later seasons of ''[[Clone Wars (disambiguation)|The Clone Wars]]'', voicing the character in three more episodes. According to an [[Ready for Battle!|interview]] with Filoni that was featured in [[Star Wars Insider 115|''Star Wars Insider'' 115]], the name "Pre" is a title of stature, like "pre-eminent," while the "Vizsla" name came from [[Tor Vizsla]], the original leader of Death Watch who was featured in the [[2002]] [[Star Wars: Jango Fett: Open Seasons|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series. Vizsla was given an entry in the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia|''The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia'']] book, released in June 2010.{{SWArchive|url=kids/read/books20091223/index.html|text=Inside ''The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia''}} He was also featured in [[Hasbro]]'s 2010 toy figure line.{{SWArchive|url=vault/collecting/news20100223.html|text=Hasbro Toy Fair Round Up!}} A concept art model sheet that was [[The Art of Mandalore|published]] in [[Star Wars Insider 116|''Star Wars Insider'' 116]] indicated that Vizsla's name was originally spelled "Visla." On the same model sheet, the symbol on his cape was depicted as the [[Mythosaur]], suggesting that the symbol was originally that of the Mandalorians and was adjusted to the shriek-hawk for the final version of "The Mandalore Plot."{{InsiderCite|116|The Art of Mandalore}} Because "Voyage of Temptation" was produced with the television series' [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]], well before the other installments in the Mandalorian story arc, the character model used for Vizsla in the episode was based on the [[Phase I clone trooper armor/Legends|Phase I clone trooper armor]] design—disguised only by his serape—instead of the finalized character design used in the later episodes.{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/voyage-of-temptation-episode-guide|text="Voyage of Temptation"
